text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- The cost of a seven-year-long real-estate crisis in France is estimated at up to 200 billion francs for the French financial sector, according to a study by the newspaper.
-- New head of navy shipyards Rodolphe Greif sees defence electronics group Thomson-CSF and navy shipyards as complementary.
-- Mobile telephone operator Bouygues Telecom to implement price-cuts policy, announces operating agreement with British, Swiss, German and Monaco-based carriers.

-- Bank of France and supervisory banking commission ask finance ministry to seek a solution for Credit Foncier de France, currently operating below normal solvency levels after a derogation of the supervisory banking authority.
-- Media group Havas does not rule out seeking an American shareholder, chairman Pierre Dauzier says in an interview, to develop international activity.
-- European Airbus consortium ARBU.PA seeks an engine for long-haul aircraft A340-600. Rolls-Royce Plc in association with French SNECMA may be chosen as suppliers.
-- EU authorities to launch on Wednesday an investigation into French state help to insurer GAN.
-- EDF utility seeks to achieve 30 percent of its activity outside France through the next ten years, chairman Edmond Alphandery says.
-- Compagnie des Signaux chairman Yazid Sabeg says is interestd in buying a 64 percent stake in Cisi held by parent company CEA-Industrie.
